items.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014
items.q: Then after that, soon, like two days after, he called me and had a gig at Knickerbocker. That’s when it just happened. And I played Knickerbocker and after we played two days he asked me to be the regular bass player.

ctx.x: I didn’t realize they had that kind of treatment for tourists. That’s nice. How did you get hooked up with Junior Mance?

I had a gig, Jazz At Noon it’s called. Anyway, they had every Friday at 2 p.m., every Friday they had a guest also. Just famous people. Junior Mance and so many. I think they had Tommy Flanagan, he was one of the guests. And he used to bring his own bass. But at that time the bass player couldn’t make it, so I started to play with him. The first time I played with him it kind of clicked. And already I was living in New York over twenty years. But I never spoke with Junior, and Junior asked me, “how long you have…

Nice. Well someone asked last night, a student sort of asked a question about why are some musicians really compatible from the start almost. Can you answer that? Why a bass player and a piano player can really work together right from the beginning.
